title: DAX measures: counts, sums and period comparisons

videos.script: Lesson 15 built a model, with four tables and three lines between them. Now it needs numbers. {{model}} You could drag Revenue into a pivot table and let Excel add it up, and that works once. A measure is better: a formula with a name, written once, that every pivot table can use. {{measure}} A measure has no fixed answer. It is worked out again for every cell of the pivot table. In the Cerrado row and the 2025 column, it adds up the Cerrado sales of 2025. One row down, it adds up other sales. {{context}} Those filters are called the filter context, and this lesson is about them. You count rows and customers, and you divide one total by another so that a ratio comes out right. {{basics}} Then comes CALCULATE, the function that changes the filters before it adds. It gives you online revenue on every row, and a channel's share of the total. {{calculate}} Then the comparisons a manager asks for: the year so far, the same period last year, and the growth between them. And the trap, because this year has six months of sales and last year has twelve. {{time}} Last, you check. Every measure is put beside a SUMIFS from lesson 5, and the two have to agree. {{check}}
